PullRequest.Title: Add a new rendering technique for whitespace
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #49462
Fixes #96976
Together with https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/168727 , fixes #111816
Fixes #149897

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The event-to-render path and full viewport loops are explicit, and the existing visible-line renderer proves prior reuse. Exact frame-time impact varies with viewport width, line length, and whitespace mode, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and transient strings/Position/range objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On each scrollTop event, cost grows with every character and rendered whitespace across the entire visible viewport, rather than only with lines entering the viewport.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased per-frame CPU/GC pressure and dropped frames during wheel or smooth scrolling.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Whitespace was serialized inside ViewLine. During overlapping vertical scrolls, ViewLayerRenderer laid out reused lines and rendered whitespace only for newly entering or otherwise invalid lines, so stable visible lines did not rebuild their whitespace markup.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new overlay marks itself dirty for every vertical scroll; prepareRender then refetches all visible line data, scans each visible line, resolves each qualifying whitespace position, and rebuilds every line's SVG/font string before unchanged strings are compared.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 83 (`return e.scrollTopChanged`) newly invalidates WhitespaceOverlay on every vertical scroll, placing its full-viewport preparation loop on the scroll-frame path.
Findings.Title: Cache whitespace output across vertical scroll frames
Findings.Impact: With renderWhitespace set to all/boundary/trailing (or a large selection), scrolling a viewport containing many long or whitespace-heavy lines repeats O(visible characters + visible whitespace) work every frame and can make scrolling visibly janky.
Findings.Evidence: The added onScrollChanged returns true for any scrollTop change. prepareRender consequently loops viewportData.startLineNumber..endLineNumber (lines 99-131), and _applyRenderWhitespace scans each line and concatenates markup per whitespace (lines 176-233). ViewOverlayLine's later _renderedContent equality check only avoids DOM replacement; it does not avoid this preparation. In contrast, ViewLayerRenderer._renderUntouchedLines only calls layoutLine on overlapping ViewLines and creates/renders lines entering the viewport.
Findings.Recommendation: Retain whitespace results per view line/content/options and recompute only entering or invalidated lines; pure scrollTop changes should reuse cached output while the visible-line layer updates positions.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop and repository call chain directly prove per-whitespace geometry reads on non-fast cache misses. Magnitude depends on how often affected line shapes and whitespace modes occur, which is reflected in medium severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous DOM geometry reads (`getBoundingClientRect`, `offsetWidth`, and Range.getClientRects`) plus one position/range allocation chain per whitespace
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold measurement cost grows linearly with qualifying whitespace in newly rendered or invalidated non-fast visible lines; long, proportional-font, Unicode/RTL, or decorated lines can require tens or hundreds of DOM range reads apiece.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked editor render/input latency and potential typing or scrolling jank from synchronous layout/geometry work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The stable ViewLine renderer emitted whitespace glyphs while serializing the line and computed offsets from its character/visible-column state; it did not perform a DOM geometry query for each whitespace glyph.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: For every whitespace selected for rendering, the overlay asks ViewLines for a visible range after text lines have been written to the DOM.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 214 introduces one `visibleRangeForPosition` call for each qualifying whitespace; before this PR whitespace rendering stayed inside renderViewLine and had no per-glyph DOM measurement boundary.
Findings.Title: Batch whitespace position measurements per line
Findings.Impact: Opening, scrolling in, or editing a non-fast line with many spaces/tabs causes the render critical path to synchronously measure each whitespace. Because overlay preparation runs immediately after ViewLines.renderText, the first geometry read can also force pending layout before the frame can complete.
Findings.Evidence: The added call at line 214 runs inside the per-character loop. RenderingContext delegates it to ViewLines.visibleRangeForPosition, which creates a new DomReadingContext for each call. For RenderedViewLine cache misses, _actualReadPixelOffset calls RangeUtil.readHorizontalRanges; that invokes Range.getClientRects, while each fresh context reads the view's getBoundingClientRect and offsetWidth. FastRenderedViewLine avoids DOM reads, but realistic non-fast cases include lines >=300 characters, non-basic/RTL text, proportional fonts, and foreign inline elements.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve whitespace coordinates in one per-line batch using a shared DOM-reading context, or expose/reuse the rendered line's character mapping and font metrics; avoid invoking the single-position DOM API once per glyph.

Scenarios.Scenario: Vertical wheel or smooth scrolling with renderWhitespace set to all, boundary, trailing, or a large selection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each scrollTop event schedules the editor UI render; WhitespaceOverlay.prepareRender must synchronously finish scanning and rebuilding output for all visible lines before the frame renders.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve rendered horizontal positions; cold non-fast positions transitively call DOM bounding-box and Range.getClientRects APIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one call per qualifying visible whitespace per frame; actual DOM reads occur for cold offsets on non-fast lines, while fast monospace lines use arithmetic and warm slow-line offsets use their pixel cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Whitespace stayed in ViewLine markup; overlapping lines were reused and only newly entering/invalid lines rendered, with no whitespace-specific position boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous during overlay preparation before the scroll frame can complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of characters and qualifying whitespace glyphs in the visible viewport on every scroll frame, not the whole document; line virtualization does not reduce work to newly entering lines in the new overlay.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully serialized on the editor/browser UI render loop; no limiter or parallel work applies.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Viewport output is rebuilt despite stable content; only downstream DOM replacement is coalesced by string equality. Geometry offsets can become warm per line, but there is no per-line whitespace-output cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added scroll invalidation, viewport loops, and existing visible-line reuse path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame cost depends on viewport dimensions, line lengths, whitespace mode, and whether visible lines use the fast rendered-line implementation.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: the diff moves full visible-viewport whitespace reconstruction onto every vertical-scroll frame.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial rendering, scrolling a new line into view, or editing a non-fast line containing many spaces/tabs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ViewLines first writes changed/new text DOM; WhitespaceOverlay then synchronously resolves every qualifying whitespace position before overlay markup can be committed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Per-position browser geometry measurement using getBoundingClientRect, offsetWidth, and Range.getClientRects on cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One visibleRangeForPosition invocation per qualifying whitespace; for each cold non-fast column, one Range.getClientRects call, with a fresh DomReadingContext that can also read parent geometry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old whitespace path serialized glyphs in renderViewLine using character and visible-column state and did not measure each whitespace through DOM geometry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks initial render, the frame exposing a new line, or the keystroke render; the first post-write geometry read can force pending layout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is qualifying whitespace count in cold or invalidated non-fast visible lines. A long prose/code line can contain tens or hundreds of positions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All geometry reads are sequential on the UI thread inside the per-character loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fast basic monospace lines avoid DOM reads. Non-fast LTR lines cache measured pixel offsets until the line is recreated; newly rendered or edited lines are cold, and RTL lines lack the pixel-offset cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete added call chain to concrete browser geometry APIs is present in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prevalence depends on configured fonts and line shapes; realistic slow cases include long lines, non-basic/RTL content, proportional fonts, and foreign inline elements.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous UI-work regression due to per-whitespace DOM measurements.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cursor and selection changes with the default renderWhitespace='selection'
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cursor events synchronously prepare overlay output before rendering when selection whitespace is enabled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Position geometry lookup for whitespace inside selected ranges.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lookup per qualifying selected whitespace; empty cursor selections cause lines to return before character scanning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Selection whitespace was handled inside invalidated ViewLines rather than a separate geometry overlay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can affect selection-drag frames for large selected ranges; covered by the submitted per-whitespace geometry finding.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible line count times active selection count, plus characters/whitespace only on lines intersecting non-empty selections.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on the UI render loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No overlay-output cache; geometry cache behavior matches the rendered-line fast/slow cases. Empty selections avoid the character loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for reachability and cardinality; lower magnitude for ordinary empty-cursor movement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large selected ranges are less common than ordinary cursor movement, and empty cursors take the early return.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: its costly mechanism is already covered by the geometry finding, while empty selections avoid the dominant loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Whitespace rendering disabled and editor option/font configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The overlay participates in editor configuration rendering, but prepareRender immediately exits when renderWhitespace is none or experimental rendering is off.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configuration events and visible overlay line count; no content-character multiplicity when whitespace is disabled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized UI work with no parallel boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: WhitespaceOptions equality suppresses overlay invalidation when relevant values are unchanged except layout changes; disabled mode stores a null render result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the explicit early return and option equality check.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable performance regression. The added applyFontInfo style writes are infrequent and do not establish meaningful user-visible cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 8 changed files and all diff pages. Reported full-viewport whitespace reconstruction on every vertical scroll and per-whitespace synchronous DOM geometry on cold/invalid non-fast lines. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries are touched.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
